To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PPARα and peroxisomal AOX are required for normal hepatic lipid metabolism.
PPARα and peroxisomal fatty acid β-oxidase are required for normal hepatic lipid metabolism.

mice deficient for both PPAR-α and AOX are free of spontaneous peroxisomal proliferation and steatosis, and the severity of steatohepatits in AOX-/- mice is enhanced by the hyperactivity of the PPAR-α signaling pathway.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of peroxisomes in lipid metabolism, and how peroxisomal dysfunction leads to fatty liver disease.
the role of PPARα and fatty acyl-Co A oxidase in fatty acid β-oxidations and their role in the pathogenesis and progression of fatty liver disease in mice.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate the metabolism and toxicity of fatty acids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lack of PPARα and the lack of AOX are both required to prevent the development of microvesicular fatty change.

mice nullizigous for both PPAα and AOX exhibit no peroxisome or mitochondrial proliferation and no steatosis, suggesting that the PPARα- AOX axis is critical in the pathogenesis and severity of fatty liver disease.
PPARα and fatty acid β-oxidase (FAO) are critical regulators of hepatic lipid homeostasis and that their coordinated action is required to maintain a normal hepatic lipid metabolism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the lack of peroxisomes in AOX−/ − mice is associated with the induction of PPARa, which in turn induces the expression of CYP4As that generate toxic DCAs, which in turn induce peroxisome formation in a compensatory manner.

the absence of per-oxisomal β–oxidation in AOX−/– mice results in increased hepatic lipid content, which is further enhanced in AOX−/- PPARα–/– mice due to the absence of PPARα–dependent CYP4A–induced dicarboxy-late acid (DCA) formation and mitochondrial β–oxidation.
the PPARα−AOX−− mouse is an ideal model for understanding the role of PPARα and fatty acyl-Coa oxidase in the pathogenesis and treatment of hepatic steatosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
peroxisomal and mitochondrial fatty acid β-oxidations are not redundant and that the two pathways are regulated differently.
PPARα and peroxisomal AOX are essential to prevent fatty liver in mice and humans.

peroxisomal fatty acid β-oxidative capacity is critical for the maintenance of hepatic lipid homeostasis and that peroxisome biogenesis is a critical determinant of the severity of microvesicular fatty liver in AOX−/deficient mice.
